goal: Build a real-time notification system: design the data model, implement the API and frontend hook, write tests, then deploy to production
summary: The collaboration begins with the Architect Agent designing the notification data model and API contracts, followed by the Coder Agent implementing the backend API and frontend hook. The Test Agent validates correctness through unit and integration tests, and finally the Deployment Agent ships the system to production. This sequential handoff ensures each layer builds on a solid foundation before proceeding.

leadAgent.responsibility: Design the notification data model (e.g., Notification schema, delivery states, user associations), define REST/WebSocket API contracts, and specify the frontend hook interface and module structure.
leadAgent.expectedOutput: A complete architecture document including: Notification data model (fields, types, relationships), API contract (endpoints, payloads, WebSocket event schemas), and frontend hook interface definition.

supportingAgents.responsibility: Implement the backend notification API (REST + WebSocket endpoints), database models, and the frontend React/JS hook for consuming real-time notifications, following the architect's contracts exactly.
supportingAgents.expectedOutput: Working backend API (notification creation, retrieval, real-time push), database migrations, and a frontend useNotifications hook with subscription logic.

supportingAgents.responsibility: Write unit tests for notification logic, integration tests for API endpoints, and end-to-end tests for the real-time WebSocket flow and frontend hook behavior.
supportingAgents.expectedOutput: Full test suite covering unit, integration, and E2E scenarios with a test report confirming passing coverage thresholds and validated correctness.

supportingAgents.responsibility: Configure CI/CD pipeline to run tests on each push, containerize the notification service with Docker, manage environment secrets, and deploy the validated build to production with health monitoring.
supportingAgents.expectedOutput: Production deployment with CI/CD pipeline configuration, Dockerfiles, environment config, and health check endpoints confirming the notification system is live.

handoffOrder.description: Architect Agent begins by designing the notification data model, defining API contracts for REST and WebSocket endpoints, and specifying the frontend hook interface and overall module structure.

handoffOrder.artifact: Architecture document: data model, API contracts, WebSocket event schema, hook interface
handoffOrder.description: Coder Agent receives the full architecture spec and implements the backend notification API, database models/migrations, WebSocket server logic, and the frontend useNotifications hook.

handoffOrder.artifact: Implemented backend API, database layer, WebSocket service, and frontend hook codebase
handoffOrder.description: Test Agent writes and executes unit tests for notification business logic, integration tests for all API endpoints, and E2E tests simulating real-time notification delivery through the WebSocket and frontend hook.

handoffOrder.artifact: Validated codebase with passing test suite and coverage report
handoffOrder.description: Deployment Agent sets up the CI/CD pipeline (running the test suite on each commit), builds Docker containers for the notification service, configures production environment variables and secrets, and deploys to production with health monitoring enabled.

risks.description: WebSocket scalability under high concurrency — a single WebSocket server may become a bottleneck with many simultaneous connections in production.
risks.mitigation: Architect Agent should design the system with a pub/sub broker (e.g., Redis Pub/Sub) to enable horizontal scaling of WebSocket servers, and this should be reflected in both the implementation and deployment configuration.

risks.description: API contract drift between architect's spec and coder's implementation could lead to frontend/backend mismatches.
risks.mitigation: Use a schema definition format (e.g., OpenAPI or Zod schemas) as the source of truth handed off from Architect to Coder, and have the Test Agent validate responses against the schema during integration testing.

risks.description: Flaky E2E tests for real-time WebSocket behavior due to timing and async nature of event delivery.
risks.mitigation: Test Agent should use robust async waiting strategies (e.g., event listeners with timeouts) and mock WebSocket servers where appropriate to ensure deterministic test outcomes in CI.

risks.description: Secret and environment configuration mismanagement could expose sensitive credentials or cause production misconfiguration.
risks.mitigation: Deployment Agent must use a secrets manager (e.g., Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, or CI secret variables) and never commit secrets to version control; environment parity between staging and production should be validated before release.
